title: Consolidate version fingerprints and strip compat routing shims
creator: Priya Patel
description: Background: Over multiple years we accumulated several lightweight compatibility shims in the request routing layer that translate legacy version fingerprints, queryparams, and route aliases into the modern manifest. These shims reduce friction for older customers but add cognitive overhead, increase config parsing complexity, and prevent the runtime from making deterministic kernel-selection decisions. Goal: consolidate all version fingerprint logic into a single canonical transformer that emits normalized route manifests, remove legacy route shims, and delete the compatibility translation table from the datastore. This will simplify startup code paths, reduce per-request branching, and make rollout history easier to reason about.
notes: Work split into three sub-tracts: 1) audit and canonicalization (fingerprint normalization rules, canonical manifest schema), 2) migrate live routing traffic to transformer-based manifests with a compatibility toggle, 3) sweep and delete the translation table + remove shims. We will keep a feature-flagged rollback path for 2 weeks after full cutover. Decision: prefer single-pass migration that rewrites stored manifests to canonical form to avoid long-term compatibility checks at runtime. Trade-offs: upfront migration cost and potential short window of admin churn vs. long-term lowered CPU/latency variance and simpler codebase.
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Kickoff doc and audit spreadsheet uploaded to Confluence (link below). Assigned engineers and identified dataset of 1.2M manifest entries that include legacy fingerprints.
2025-02-20: Prototype transformer implemented in runtime-v2 branch; unit tests for normalization rules added. Observed 4% CPU improvement on microbenchmarks when shims are bypassed.
2025-02-26: Infra scheduled small migration window for 2025-03-05 to rewrite manifests in staging. Migration tool can apply canonicalization in batches and snapshot before change.
2025-03-01: Design review complete; PM approved rollout plan. Security reviewed migration tool I/O; no sensitive fields modified. Obtained ops signoff on rollback SLOs.
2025-03-03: Began canary migration against 10k manifests in staging; observed no observable request regression. Continuing incremental migration and telemetry collection.
acceptance_criteria: All request routing code paths reference the canonical manifest schema (no conditional legacy shims remain)
Compatibility translation table removed from datastore and backup snapshot stored in long-term archive
End-to-end tests exercise both new transformer and rollback toggle; zero customer-facing errors in canary and staged rollouts
Benchmarks show CPU or latency variance reduced (>=2% improvement on 95th percentile token latency for small models)
Documentation updated: Console docs, admin runbooks, and migration playbook available in Confluence
steps: Audit existing fingerprints and aliases; publish canonicalization rules (Confluence)
Merge transformer implementation behind a feature flag and run internal integration tests
Run staged manifests migration in a non-prod environment and validate traces/dashboards
Enable canary toggle for small percentage of production traffic and monitor for 72 hours
If stable, schedule rolling migration of stored manifests with short maintenance windows; keep rollback toggle active
Remove shims and compatibility config; run full test suite and static analysis
Delete translation table from primary datastore and move backup to archive bucket

blockers: Need final approval for maintenance window from SRE (awaiting update from oncall)

qa_plan: End-to-end QA will run a dedicated suite that replays historical requests against transformed manifests and compares outputs. Smoke tests in production after canary, and a 72-hour observation window before full rollout. Post-migration audits to sample 5% of manifests and verify canonical schema compliance.
